stories.title: Claude users found ways around safeguards for bioweapons research
stories.author: Zehra Munir, Financial Times
bullet_points: AI safety mechanisms (safeguards) for large language models like Claude have been circumvented by users.
The vulnerability stems from the difficulty in distinguishing between legitimate scientific research and dangerous bioweapons research.
This highlights a critical, emerging challenge in AI alignment and safety concerning sensitive scientific domains.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Slack is integrating AI-powered 'Slackforce Surfaces' to allow users to build complex outputs directly within chats.
The new feature enables the creation of interactive reports, dashboards, polls, and microsites using natural language prompts.
The AI leverages data from connected apps (e.g., Google Drive, Salesforce) and existing conversations to generate content.

stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Big Tech companies are actively influencing K-12 education by providing AI-related curriculum and resources to schools.
The narrative being pushed is that proficiency in these 'hot new' technologies is essential for students to remain competitive in the job market.
This trend represents a significant industry shift where tech creators are partnering with education systems to drive adoption of their platforms.

stories.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy is linked to a potential data sale to Google.
The news raises concerns about the commodification of personal data in the context of AI development.
The article critiques the trend, warning against data acquisition becoming a 'land grab' in the AI sector.

stories.title: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Addresses a known bottleneck where Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR) runs faster on CPUs than GPUs.
Proposes GPU-CFR, a method that achieves an 80x speedup by compiling the game to static dataflow and using CUDA Graph replay.
Focuses on overcoming overhead from kernel launches and framework dispatch, which dominate runtime in prior GPU implementations.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address gaps in standard marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM incorporates metrics like repeated answers, question counts, and notice probabilities to quantify AI-driven marketing effectiveness.

stories.title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI
stories.author: Yakov Pyotr Shkolnikov
bullet_points: Addresses the control problem in Agentic AI as systems move beyond single tasks to maintain consequential state.
Proposes an 'artificial id' as an adaptive internal drive to manage when AI behavior should continue, stop, or change.
This work aims to automate behavioral transitions currently requiring manual, external specification (objectives, retries, stopping rules).

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in LLMs, addressing unfaithful claims.
The pipeline combines DeBERTa-v3 classification, MC Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for general-domain tasks.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address gaps in standard marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM integrates complex metrics like notice probabilities and shares of use across various generative systems.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs).
The detection method combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for general-domain hallucination detection.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI to continuously enhance its own capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression toward advanced autonomy, culminating in recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a novel multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in LLMs, combining DeBERTa-v3, MC Dropout, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance on the HaluEval benchmark, demonstrating F1=0.915 and AUROC=0.977 on general tasks.
Focuses specifically on domain-specific hallucination detection, addressing the issue of unfaithful claims in fluent LLM output.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: rustfoundation.org via mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has officially designated Rust as a Tier-1 language within its development ecosystem.
This signifies a major corporate endorsement and increased investment in Rust's adoption for critical systems.
The move reflects a broader industry trend towards using memory-safe languages to mitigate security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-source LLM ecosystems (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models across various hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving functionality on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Why Apple’s next computer should be for the smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Apple's new direction seems to favor an 'intelligent personal hub' over traditional hardware announcements.
The focus of this hub is heavily placed on local processing and enhanced user privacy.
The initial keynote emphasized this concept while discussing the iPhone, suggesting a broader ecosystem shift.

stories.title: Insta360 launches a single-lens Osmo Pocket rival you can actually buy in the US
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Insta360 has released the Luna Ultra Pro, a single-lens compact steadycam competing with DJI's Osmo Pocket line.
The key differentiator for the Luna Ultra Pro is its ability to shoot vertical video in 4K.
This release follows the initial launch of the two-lens Luna Ultra, signaling a strategic move in the action camera market.

stories.title: ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new malware strain named ClickFix is actively infecting both Windows PCs and Macs.
The malware's success is attributed to its simple nature combined with user frustration.
The viral spread indicates a significant, current cybersecurity threat across major operating systems.

stories.title: Rocket Report: Europe joins the commercial launch club; a Ravn X sighting?
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Europe is entering the commercial space launch sector.
The report mentions a potential sighting of a 'Ravn X' vehicle.
The article suggests increased investment or focus on the space industry.

stories.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: LinkedIn successfully defended against lawsuits concerning its scanning of users' Chrome extensions.
The court dismissed the lawsuits, finding that the plaintiffs failed to allege a genuine privacy violation.
This ruling addresses legal challenges related to how LinkedIn interacts with browser extensions.

stories.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: Europe is pursuing an independent Venus mission due to NASA's withdrawal of a radar instrument.
The situation reflects broader trends of NASA potentially canceling international partnerships.
Europe is exploring potential collaborations, including with China, for the mission.

stories.title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Android now supports secure migration of login credentials between password managers.
This feature aims to improve user convenience and security across different password management apps.
Current app support is limited, but Google plans to expand compatibility in the future.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new theoretical concept, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to handle mismatches between source and target data supports.
Bridges the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical applicability using entropic optimal transport.

stories.title: Can Edge-Deployable Vision-Language Models Identify Species?
stories.author: Yi Ding
bullet_points: The research focuses on the practical application of small, edge-deployable Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for real-world tasks like species identification in remote camera trap settings.
The study evaluates the taxonomic knowledge embedded in VLMs within the 2B-8B parameter range (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Gemma3 4B) against a specialized model (BioCLIP).
This work addresses the critical need for efficient, locally-run AI solutions in environments with limited connectivity, moving beyond frontier-scale models.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: MindTopo introduces a new benchmark to test foundation models on topological reasoning, moving beyond traditional metric properties.
The research highlights that true spatial understanding requires recognizing topological relations (invariant under deformation), which current evaluations often miss.
The benchmark is grounded in cognitive science and formal topology, focusing on properties like continuity.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper introduces Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to persistently enhance their own capabilities and improvement processes.
It utilizes the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The proposed RSI roadmap outlines a progression through stages, culminating in recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new theoretical concept, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to handle mismatches between source and target data supports.
Bridges the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical applicability using entropic optimal transport.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of data repetition on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a key area where prior research focused on dense Transformers.
Addresses the practical issue of data scarcity in modern NLP, where training data is often reused.
Examines how data repetition affects MoE performance across varying repetition rates and model configurations.

stories.title: From Protocols to Evidence: Bounded Claims for AI in Service of the Common Good
stories.author: Paulo Benanti
bullet_points: AI deployment is not just a governance issue but a diagnostic tool for existing institutional failures (e.g., lack of care, accountability).
AI acts as an intervention, capable of repairing, compounding, substituting for, or concealing these pre-existing institutional ruptures.
Responsible AI frameworks must move beyond abstract principles to concrete protocols that evaluate both the AI system and the institutional context.

stories.title: CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era
stories.author: Han-Jia Ye
bullet_points: The paper introduces CausalArena, a new benchmarking suite for causal discovery methods.
Causal discovery is highlighted as crucial for scientific reasoning and intervention-based decision-making.
The evaluation is complicated by the rise of Causal Discovery Foundation Models (CDFMs), necessitating standardized protocols.

stories.title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Rajalakshmi Nandakumar
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) for mmWave radar, a complex problem requiring physical fidelity and complex-valued rendering.
Existing methods struggle to simultaneously achieve physical faithfulness, complex-valued output, and multi-viewpoint tractability for radar data.
The proposed solution utilizes 3D Point Splatting, an advancement that aims to overcome the scaling limitations of traditional differentiable Monte Carlo ray tracers in this domain.

stories.title: CoRA-NAS: Coarse Ranking and Anchor-Residual Refinement for Neural Architecture Search
stories.author: Jiaojiao Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces CoRA-NAS, a two-stage framework for Neural Architecture Search (NAS).
Combines a static ranking prior (CoRA-Rank) with low-cost learning-curve refinement (CoRA-Refine).
Addresses the reliability issues of zero-cost proxies in architecture search by using consensus mechanisms and anchor extrapolation.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: The research investigates the impact of repeating language model training data, a growing practice due to data scarcity.
It specifically examines this phenomenon in sparse architectures like Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), an area less studied than dense Transformers.
The study analyzes how data repetition affects MoE models across different repetition rates and domain mixes.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: Introduces MindTopo, a new benchmark designed to test topological reasoning in foundation models.
Highlights the gap in current AI evaluations, which primarily focus on metric properties (distance, shape) rather than topological invariants.
Aims to bridge cognitive science insights on spatial understanding with formal topology within large language models.

stories.title: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs
stories.author: Muhammad Alqurishi
bullet_points: Addresses the significant underrepresentation of Arabic in multilingual Speech Large Language Models (speech-LLMs).
Introduces Nuha-Speech, a comprehensive initiative focused on developing general-purpose Arabic speech-LLMs.
The project covers the entire lifecycle, including dataset construction, model training, and systematic evaluation, specifically focusing on Arabic Speech Question-Answering (SQA).

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to autonomously enhance their capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The development roadmap for RSI progresses through stages, culminating in recursive meta-improvement and various levels of autonomy.

stories.title: RetroThinker: Enabling Retrospective Thinking in Speech LLMs
stories.author: David Harwath
bullet_points: Introduces 'RetroThinker' to improve complex reasoning in Speech LLMs.
Addresses the gap where SpeechLLMs lag behind text-only LLMs in reasoning, despite offering lower latency than cascaded ASR/LM systems.
Focuses on enhancing reasoning capabilities while adhering to strict real-time latency constraints required for spoken interaction.

stories.title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
stories.author: fnthawar2
bullet_points: Shopify is undergoing a significant platform technology shift.
The company is migrating away from React Native.
The new native development stack will utilize Swift and Kotlin.

stories.title: Forgejo 16.0.4 has a critical security bug fix (RCE - Remote Code Execution)
stories.author: codeberg.org via brn
bullet_points: Forgejo, a self-hosted Git service, has released version 16.0.4.
The update addresses a critical security vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as Remote Code Execution (RCE), requiring immediate attention from users.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is achieving coding proficiency surpassing many human developers.
It argues that coding itself is not the most valuable skill in software development.
The discussion suggests a shift in the value proposition of human developers away from pure coding.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation is accelerating rapidly.
The primary challenge is not generation speed, but ensuring code correctness.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in AI-assisted software development.

stories.title: AI-Generated Tests Can Make Coding Agents Worse. Here's How to Check Yours
stories.author: p0rt
bullet_points: AI-generated tests can negatively impact the performance of coding agents.
Research (ExecCritic) demonstrated that weak generated tests lead to lower repair success rates.
The article provides a practical Python example to help developers validate and catch faulty fixes approved by inadequate tests.

stories.title: Most AI "Reasoning" Traces Are Just the Answer, Written Backwards
stories.author: dj29
bullet_points: The article critiques the common visualization of AI 'reasoning' chains.
It suggests that many step-by-step outputs are merely the final answer presented in reverse order.
This points to a potential superficiality in current LLM explanation mechanisms.
